newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Thai worries continue to strangle Singapore shares.
newsitem.headline: Thai worries continue to strangle Singapore shares.

text.p: Singapore shares were down at Friday's lunchtime break, hit by continuing concerns about exposure in Thailand following Thursday's baht crisis, dealers said.
"We can expect some more volatility in the market throughout the day because of that," one dealer at a local firm said.
The Straits Times Industrials Index was off 13.58 points or 0.66 percent to 2,056.16 by lunchtime close.
Dealers said prices were depressed more by baht fears than Singapore's weak first quarter economic data released on Friday.
"There was no surprise from the GDP figures and reaction has been minimal," one dealer said.
Blue chips were the main victims in a light morning session which saw just 59 million shares traded and produced 151 losers to 101 gainers.
City Developments led losers down Singapore $0.60 at S$12.70. Singapore Press foreign was off S$0.50 at S$28.00.
Top actives were Malaysian stocks MBF Capital and MBF Holdings, traded over the counter in Singapore.
Both were up a cent at S$2.26 and S$0.725 respectively.
